# Conservative Party 2024 Manifesto Summary

## Economic Foundation and Tax Cuts
The Conservatives highlight their economic recovery following COVID-19 and the Ukraine conflict, with inflation reduced and growth returning. Central to their platform are substantial tax cuts: halving employee National Insurance from 12% to 6% by April 2027 (saving average workers £1,350), abolishing self-employed National Insurance entirely, and introducing the "Triple Lock Plus" to protect pensioner incomes from income tax. They commit to not raising income tax, VAT, or Capital Gains Tax.

## Immigration and Border Security
The party pledges to introduce a legally binding migration cap that falls annually, with parliamentary oversight. They promise to continue Rwanda deportation flights, reform international asylum rules, and implement stricter visa requirements including health checks for migrants. They emphasise stopping illegal Channel crossings through deterrence.

## Defence and National Security
Defence spending will increase to 2.5% of GDP by 2030, representing the largest sustained investment since the Cold War. This includes £10 billion for munitions production, continued support for Ukraine, and modernisation of armed forces through AI and new technologies. They will maintain the Trident nuclear deterrent and establish a National Defence and Resilience Plan.

## Housing and Infrastructure
The Conservatives target 1.6 million new homes by abolishing EU "nutrient neutrality" rules, prioritising brownfield development, and protecting the Green Belt. First-time buyers will benefit from permanent Stamp Duty relief up to £425,000 and a new Help to Buy scheme. Infrastructure investment includes £36 billion from HS2 savings for regional transport projects.

## Healthcare and Public Services
NHS spending will increase above inflation annually, with plans for 92,000 more nurses and 28,000 more doctors. The manifesto emphasises technological transformation, expanded Pharmacy First services, and 50 new Community Diagnostic Centres. Mental health support will expand to all schools by 2030.

## Other Key Policies
- Mandatory National Service for 18-year-olds (military or civic)
- Mobile phone bans in schools
- 100,000 new apprenticeships funded by closing poor-quality university courses
- 8,000 additional neighbourhood police officers
- Protection of biological sex in the Equality Act
- £1 billion increase to UK farming budget
